From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed mutual action plan so we have alignment on scope, stakeholders, and next milestones. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Inference latency spikes during peak traffic causing user-facing timeouts (~95th percentile > 500ms).
- Per-token inference cost is higher than expected given scale; looking to reduce unit costs by ~40–60%.
- Need a deployment option that keeps PII inside your VPC for regulated datasets.
- Lack of reliable rollout / canary tooling when switching model versions.

Goals you want to achieve (measurable):
1) 95th percentile latency < 200ms for production queries.
2) Reduce inference unit cost by ~50% compared to current provider.
3) Private deployment (VPC) for PII workflows and SOC2 evidence for security review.
4) Predictable rollouts and automated fallbacks to prevent outages during model updates.

Mutual Action Plan (draft milestones & dates) — proposed owners:
- Discovery sign-off: confirm success criteria (you) — target: 2026-06-17
- PoC start (dedicated capacity + 1 model): engineering setup & sample data — target: 2026-06-20
- Security questionnaire + evidence delivery (KMS, audit logs, data residency): security teams — target: 2026-06-28
- Procurement / commercial review & SOW sign: procurement / legal — target: 2026-07-05
- Production rollout & SLA go-live: joint ops — target: 2026-07-20

Stakeholders we have on record:
- Priya Singh — CTO (decision-maker)
- Alex Johnson — Product Lead (technical buyer)
- Daniel Reed — Procurement (you to confirm)

Decision process and timeline:
- Technical PoC validated by product & engineering (1–2 weeks).
- Security review runs in parallel (1 week).
- Executive approval after PoC & security sign-off (~1 week).

Action items / asks for Acme:
1) Please confirm procurement contact (we expect a procurement/legal lead we can loop in).
2) Confirm PoC start date of 2026-06-20 works for your engineering team.
3) Share any required security templates or a point of contact for SOC2 evidence collection.

Attached: 20260610-acme-map-draft.pdf — a one-page MAP we discussed (milestones, owners, risks).

If that looks good, I’ll circulate an updated MAP & SOW and loop in our security engineer for a kickoff.

Best,

Marissa Cole
